examples.ko: 어릴 때 우리 집은 많이 가난했어요.
examples.en: My family was very poor when I was little.
I joined a group that helps poor people.
Even though we were poor, the family lived happily.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 가난하게 자랐지만 열심히 노래했어요.
examples.en: That singer grew up poor but sang with all her heart.
Being poor is no reason to give up on your dreams too.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 가난해서 학교에 못 간 아이도 많았어요.
examples.en: In the old days many children couldn't go to school because they were poor.

explain: '가난하다'는 사람이나 집안의 형편 전체를 말해서 조금 무겁게 들려요. 지금 돈이 없을 때는 '돈이 없어요'나 '형편이 어려워요'가 자연스러워요. 반대말은 '부유하다'인데, 입말에서는 '부자예요', '잘살아요'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: We were poor, so it was hard to go to school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form used to give a reason.

phrases.example: 요즘 형편이 어려워서 여행을 못 가요.
phrases.en: Money is tight these days, so I can't travel.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가난하다'보다 덜 무겁고 지금 상황을 부드럽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than 'gananhada', describing the current situation.
phrases.en_equiv: to be in a tight situation

phrases.example: 우리 집은 가난하지 않지만 부자도 아니에요.
phrases.en: My family isn't poor, but we're not rich either.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가난하다'의 부정형으로, 형편이 그렇게 나쁘지 않다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form of 'gananhada', used to say one's situation is not that bad.

explain_en: '가난하다' describes a person's or family's whole situation, so it sounds heavy. When you just have no money right now, '돈이 없어요' or '형편이 어려워요' is more natural. The opposite is '부유하다', but in speech people say '부자예요' or '잘살아요'.

examples.en: I had warm gomtang for lunch.
Gomtang is made by boiling beef bones for a long time.

examples.ko: 곰탕에 소금과 파를 넣어 간을 맞춰요.
examples.en: You season gomtang by adding salt and green onion.
This restaurant is really famous for its gomtang.
One bowl of gomtang here, please.
Gomtang and kkakdugi go really well together.

explain: 소고기와 뼈를 오래 끓인 뽀얗고 맑은 국이에요. 식당에서는 보통 깍두기와 함께 나와요. '설렁탕'과 비슷한 음식으로 같이 파는 식당도 많아요.

phrases.en: One bowl of gomtang, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 주문할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: What you say when ordering at a restaurant.

phrases.en: My mother has been boiling gomtang since the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국을 오래 끓여 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means making the soup by boiling it for a long time.

phrases.en: A new gomtang restaurant opened near my office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곰탕을 파는 식당을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A restaurant that sells gomtang.

explain_en: It is a clear, milky soup made by boiling beef and bones for a long time. At restaurants it usually comes with kkakdugi (radish kimchi). It is similar to '설렁탕', and many restaurants sell both.

examples.en: I fell and cracked my leg bone.

examples.ko: 다리뼈가 부러져서 한 달 동안 깁스했어요.
examples.en: I broke my leg bone and wore a cast for a month.
I had my leg bone X-rayed.
The child's leg bones are still growing.
There is a fossil of a dinosaur leg bone in the museum.
The length of leg bones differs slightly from person to person.

explain: 다리에 있는 뼈를 통틀어 부르는 말이에요. 병원에서 구체적으로 말할 때는 '정강이뼈'처럼 부위 이름을 쓰기도 해요. 뼈가 '부러지다', '금이 가다'와 자주 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I broke my leg bone while skiing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뼈가 완전히 부러졌을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the bone is completely broken.

phrases.en: I heard he fell and cracked his leg bone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부러지지는 않았지만 갈라졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the bone is cracked but not broken through.

phrases.en: I hurt my shin bone while playing soccer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다리뼈 중에서 무릎 아래 앞쪽 뼈를 구체적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A specific bone in the lower leg, below the knee.

explain_en: It is a general word for the bones of the leg. At a hospital people may use specific names such as '정강이뼈' (shinbone). It often goes with '부러지다' (break) and '금이 가다' (crack).

examples.en: The bathwater temperature is just right.

examples.ko: 목욕물이 너무 뜨거워서 찬물을 조금 섞었어요.
examples.en: The bathwater was too hot, so I mixed in a little cold water.

examples.ko: 아이를 위해 따뜻한 목욕물을 받아 놓았어요.
examples.en: I ran some warm bathwater for the child.
I put a little salt in the bathwater and I feel refreshed.
Get in quickly before the bathwater cools down.
I forgot to drain the bathwater from the tub.

explain: 목욕물은 '받다'와 잘 어울려서 '목욕물을 받다'라고 말해요. 물을 뺄 때는 '빼다'를 써요. '목욕물 온도'처럼 온도를 말할 때도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I run the bath in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 욕조에 물을 채운다고 할 때 '받다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 받다 for filling the tub with water.

phrases.en: I finished bathing and drained the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물을 내보낼 때는 '빼다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 빼다 for draining the water.

phrases.en: Getting into warm bathwater relieves my tiredness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 온도를 나타내는 말을 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a word for temperature in front of it.

explain_en: It pairs naturally with '받다', so you say '목욕물을 받다' for running a bath. To drain it, use '빼다'. It also often appears in phrases about temperature, like '목욕물 온도'.

en: sound of rain; sound of raindrops

examples.en: I like rain, so I like the sound of it.

examples.ko: 한옥 카페의 툇마루에서 차를 마시며 빗소리를 들었어요.
examples.en: I listened to the rain while drinking tea on the porch of a hanok cafe.
The sound of the rain kept me from sleeping well all night.
The sound of rain outside the window woke me up.
The sound of rain makes my mind feel at ease.
The smell of coffee spread along with the sound of rain.

explain: '비'와 '소리' 사이에 사이시옷이 들어가서 '빗소리'로 쓰고 [비쏘리]로 읽어요. '빗소리를 듣다', '빗소리가 들리다'로 많이 써요. 비가 오는 날의 분위기를 말할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I can hear the sound of rain outside the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 귀에 들어올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the sound reaches your ears.
phrases.en_equiv: the sound of rain is heard

phrases.en: Last night I fell asleep to the sound of rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-에'로 소리가 원인이나 배경임을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: -에 shows the sound as the cause or background.
phrases.en_equiv: to fall asleep to the rain

phrases.en: It's raining hard, so the rain sounds loud.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리의 크기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe how loud the sound is.

explain_en: An 사이시옷 sits between '비' and '소리', so it is written '빗소리' and read [비쏘리]. Common patterns are '빗소리를 듣다' and '빗소리가 들리다'. It often comes up when describing the mood of a rainy day.

examples.en: This store has a sale this weekend.
The department store is having a sale on winter clothes.
I heard the shoes at that shop go on sale starting today.
I went early on the morning of the sale day.
The shop is having a sale, so there are so many people.
I asked the staff when they'd have a sale.

explain: 가게에서 값을 내려 팔 때 '세일', '세일하다'를 많이 써요. '할인하다'는 조금 더 공식적이고 '세일'은 입말이에요. '세일 중이다', '세일 기간'처럼 명사로도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: This store is having a sale right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 세일이 진행되는 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says that a sale is going on at this moment.

phrases.en: I bought a winter coat during the sale period.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세일하는 동안을 말할 때 명사로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase for the time the sale runs.

phrases.en: These shoes are 30 percent off.
phrases.nuance_ko: '세일하다'보다 조금 더 공식적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Slightly more formal than 세일하다.

explain_en: Shops use 세일 and 세일하다 a lot when lowering prices. 할인하다 sounds more formal, while 세일 is more spoken. It is also often used as a noun: 세일 중, 세일 기간.

examples.ko: 고기를 상추에 싸서 쌈장을 올려 먹어요.
examples.en: I wrap the meat in lettuce and eat it with ssamjang on top.
The ssamjang my mom makes is the best.
I added a little minced garlic to the ssamjang.

examples.ko: 쌈장은 짤 수 있으니 조금만 찍으세요.
examples.en: Ssamjang can be salty, so dip just a little.
Fresh vegetables dipped in ssamjang taste good.
I asked the pork belly restaurant for more ssamjang.

explain: '쌈'과 같이 외우면 쉬워요. 상추쌈, 깻잎쌈처럼 쌈 채소에 밥과 고기를 올리고 쌈장을 조금 얹어 먹어요. '쌈장을 찍다, 바르다, 올리다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: I dipped the green pepper in ssamjang and ate it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 채소나 고추를 장에 살짝 묻힐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when lightly dipping vegetables or peppers in the sauce.

phrases.example: 상추 위에 쌈장을 올리고 고기를 싸요.
phrases.en: I put ssamjang on the lettuce and wrap the meat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쌈 위에 장을 얹을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when putting the sauce on top of a wrap.

phrases.en: Please give me more ssamjang and lettuce.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고기를 먹을 때 함께 나오는 것들을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for items that come together when eating meat.

explain_en: Learn it with '쌈' (a wrap). You put rice and meat on a leaf such as lettuce or perilla, as in '상추쌈' and '깻잎쌈', and add a little ssamjang. You say '쌈장을 찍다' (dip), '바르다' (spread) or '올리다' (put on top).

examples.en: I like action movies the most.
The action in this game is really flashy.
Filming began when the director called out 'action'.
The lead's action acting was really cool.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 위험한 액션 장면도 직접 했어요.
examples.en: That actor did even the dangerous action scenes himself.

examples.ko: 액션과 코미디가 섞인 영화를 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to watch a movie that mixes action and comedy.

explain: 싸움이나 움직임이 많은 장면과 영화 장르를 말할 때 가장 많이 들려요. 몸짓 하나하나는 '동작'이나 '행동'이라고 해서 쓰는 자리가 달라요. 촬영장에서 감독이 시작 신호로 외치는 '액션'도 그대로 써요.

phrases.example: 그 영화는 액션 장면이 정말 멋있어요.
phrases.en: That movie has really cool action scenes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 싸우거나 달리는 움직임이 많은 장면을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Scenes with lots of fighting or running.

phrases.en: I played an action game with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠르게 움직이며 하는 게임 종류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A type of game played with fast movement.

phrases.example: 그 액션 배우는 위험한 장면도 직접 해요.
phrases.en: That action actor does even dangerous scenes himself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 싸움이나 움직임이 많은 영화에 자주 나오는 배우를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An actor who often appears in movies with lots of movement or fighting.

explain_en: Most often it names fast, fighting-heavy scenes and the movie genre. A single gesture is '동작' or '행동', so the words are not interchangeable. The director's start call on a film set is also just 'action'.

examples.en: Oh, come on, how could that be?
Oh, that much is nothing.
Ugh, late again today?
Oh, I worried about the exam for nothing.

examples.ko: 에이, 그건 너무 비싸서 못 사요.
examples.en: Aw, that is too expensive, so I can't buy it.
Oh, don't say things like that.

explain: 믿기지 않거나 아쉽고 못마땅할 때 짧게 내는 소리예요. '에이, 아니에요'처럼 가볍게 부정하거나 달랠 때도 써요. 친한 사이의 입말이라서 윗사람에게 크게 쓰면 버릇없게 들릴 수 있고, 글에서는 거의 안 써요.

phrases.example: 에이, 아니에요. 저는 그런 말 안 했어요.
phrases.en: Oh, no. I didn't say that.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에이' 뒤에 붙여서 가볍게 부정하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Added after 'ei' to deny something lightly.

phrases.en: Oh, it's nothing. It's no big deal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고맙다는 말을 들었을 때 겸손하게 대답하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modest reply when someone thanks you.

phrases.en: Oh, come on, don't be like that. Let's go together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대를 가볍게 달래거나 설득할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to gently coax or persuade someone.

explain_en: A short sound you make when you can't quite believe something, or feel let down or displeased. It also softens a denial or soothes someone, as in 'Oh, no way'. It is casual speech for close friends; to a superior it can sound rude, and it is rare in writing.

examples.en: What are you going to do this weekend?
This time I'll buy you a nice meal.
This exam was much easier than the last one.
I decided to cut spending this month.
Please help me just this once.
It was a pity that it rained on this trip.

explain: '이번'을 더 말랑하게 말하는 구어체예요. 친한 사이의 대화에서 자연스럽고, 글이나 공식적인 자리에서는 '이번'이 더 맞아요. 반대로 지나간 때는 '지난번', 다음은 '다음번'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Do you have time this week?
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에서 이번 주를 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say this week among friends.

phrases.en: I'm very busy this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이번 달'보다 말랑한 구어체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer spoken form than 'ibeon dal'.

phrases.en: Let's watch a movie together this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글이나 공식적인 자리에서는 '이번'이 더 알맞아요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Ibeon' fits writing and formal situations better.

explain_en: It is a softer, spoken version of '이번'. It sounds natural among friends, while '이번' fits writing and formal situations better. The previous one is '지난번' and the next one is '다음번'.

examples.en: On my way home from work, I got a whole fried chicken to go.
I'll order half fried and half seasoned chicken.
The fried chicken at this place is crispy and delicious.
I like fried chicken more than seasoned chicken.
This place has a special sauce for its fried chicken.
Fried chicken loses its crispiness when it cools.

explain: 그냥 '치킨'이라고 줄여 말하는 일이 많고, 말할 때는 '후라이드'라고도 해요. 주문할 때 '양념치킨'과 나눠서 고르는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: Shall we eat chicken tonight?
phrases.nuance_ko: '프라이드치킨'을 줄여 일상에서 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short form most used in daily life.

phrases.en: I like fried chicken better.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 흔히 쓰는 다른 소리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common spoken variant of the word.

phrases.en: I ordered fried chicken with my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배달로 주문할 때 '시키다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 시키다 when ordering delivery.

explain_en: People often just say '치킨', and in speech it is also pronounced '후라이드'. When ordering, you often choose between this and '양념치킨' (seasoned chicken).
